title: drillExport
body:
## drillExport

Runs the same design rule check and, only if it passes the authored maximums, exports Excellon drill files with kicad-cli pcb export drill: decimal coordinates, absolute board origin, in millimetres or inches, with plated (PTH) and non-plated (NPTH) holes in separate files or one merged file. Every drill hit is read back independently and matched one-to-one to a board hole by position, diameter and plating. Outputs are the drill files, board-summary.json, drc-report.json and board-statistics.json. Choose it to produce the drilling data a board fabricator needs alongside layer plots from KiCad.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Excellon uses a y-up frame: a hole at KiCad board position (8, 10) mm is written X8.0Y-10.0.
- Only round holes spanning F.Cu to B.Cu are supported; slots, drill offsets, backdrills, blind/buried vias and drilled pads on back-side footprints are rejected before KiCad runs.
- No drill map, drill report or Gerber job file is produced; layer plots still come from KiCad itself.

Native binding: `kicad-cli pcb export drill`. Output kind: `["drill","text"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board` | Absolute path to an existing saved .kicad_pcb file. A sibling .kicad_pro (rules, netclasses, severities) and .kicad_dru (custom rules) with the same name are captured with it; KiCad only ever sees copies inside the run directory, so the original is never modified. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}` | **required** |
| `maximumErrors` | Largest acceptable number of DRC violations with error severity (for example clearance, shorts, minimum annular width) in the native report. The run fails with DRC_VIOLATIONS when the actual count is larger; the report and summary are kept for review. Excluded violations are reported separately and never counted. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":100000}` | `0` |
| `maximumWarnings` | Largest acceptable number of DRC violations with warning severity (for example dangling tracks or silkscreen overlaps) in the native report. The run fails with DRC_VIOLATIONS when the actual count is larger; the report and summary are kept for review. Severities come from the board project; checks set to ignore are listed but not counted. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":100000}` | `0` |
| `maximumUnconnected` | Largest acceptable number of unconnected items (connections KiCad's ratsnest still shows as missing) in the native report. The run fails with DRC_VIOLATIONS when the actual count is larger; the report and summary are kept for review. Every routed net needs all of its pads connected by copper to reach zero. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":100000}` | `0` |
| `units` | Units of the coordinates and tool diameters written in the Excellon files: mm writes three decimals, in writes four. The summary and comparisons are always in millimetres. | `{"type":"enum","values":["mm","in"]}` | `"mm"` |
| `separatePlating` | Whether plated (board-PTH.drl) and non-plated (board-NPTH.drl) holes go in separate files. When false, one board.drl contains both, with each tool marked plated or non-plated. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` |
